title: Claude is helping me build my dream survival game!
author: BladenBranch
selftext:
Hey everyone! I've been using claude to help me flesh out a survival game long in the making. I've used it for animations, models, code, etc... 

I've always loved survival games but could never really get the Wurm meets somewhat modern gameplay and now I'm making it for real! The game will be available entirely for free on itch, and has a permdeath mode for real stakes, something I've always loved.  

Obviously lots of work to be done with the weird animation glitches and such, but what do we think about the fishing? Really bad hitch on the first cast that's getting fixed.

I want this to be a real dangerous game where you never truly know what can kill you and what can't and can only be learned through playing and so far it's been a blast. Claude has helped with building a true ecosystem in the game where prey are hunted by predators, they can kill out the prey and move on to other areas when they get hungry or even start killing eachother to eat. Bears can be found fishing for salmon in the rivers during salmon runs. Trolls guard their cave entrances and the overall progression is not linear at all, there's plenty of ways to progress.

Thanks for coming to my TED Talk. Happy Dev'ing!

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: Looks great! ❤️ This makes me wanna turn my little tropical island fish game demo into a survival game!

comments.author: FrankenChocula
comments.body:
Yeah, wow... the giant internet court of public opinion.. navigating that sounds like a big steaming pile of no-fun!

I think you are taking a good approach.  Just put it out there.. if people play it and like it, great.

It's this way for a lot of creations, not just games.  So much of what people create just never really gets consumed... books and stories, artwork, even the endless supply of TV shows.  I am really starting to think that sharing these smaller projects with friends and family directly to share experiences with people actually known is a more reasonable approach than dealing with all the nonsense.

Good luck!
